union: engineering-runtime-union (Hns primary implementation + Boss engineering closed loop)

donors.role: primary implementation: plan/DAG-ordering, discovery, failure classification, recovery/checkpoint, isolation, verification, result gate
union additions: the §33 recovery ladder with per-class budgets, and the CI-repair parse/classify/plan loop

adaptation: CommonJS and TypeScript -> plain ESM .mjs with JSDoc. No TypeScript, no build step, no npm dependency; `node:` built-ins and relative .mjs specifiers only.

The union is kept as a union, not a winner. `failure.mjs` is the DS-Hns vocabulary (16 lower-case classes, a class-to-action policy, and repair memory that refuses a blind retry); `failure-recovery.mjs` is the Boss vocabulary (13 upper-case classes, an evidence-driven ladder with per-class budgets, Owner escalation and the HNS fallback rule). Neither imports, re-exports nor translates the other, and both module headers spell out the overlap (`workspace`/`WORKSPACE`, `TEST` vs `unit-test`+`integration-test`, `BUILD` vs `syntax`+`type`+`compile`).

`discovery.mjs` publishes `OPERATIONS` and `CONFIDENCE` as its own frozen constants and loads `adapters.mjs` lazily, rather than importing it eagerly. Reason: `plan.mjs` needs the closed operation vocabulary to validate a step, so a module that only wants the vocabulary must not be unimportable when no adapter set is present. The list is the donor's own, and a test asserts it equals `adapters.mjs`'s export.

`process.mjs` does NOT port DS-Hns `app/computer-use/{processes,errors}.cjs`, which are Computer-Use-domain and out of this Mission's scope. The donor's supervisor already accepts an injected registry, so `createProcessSupervisor` keeps that seam and falls back to a minimal local registry implementing exactly the surface the supervisor consumes — the shape demonstrated by the donor's own test helper `tests/helpers/engineering-scripted.cjs`: `snapshot()` returning `{ownedCount, owned, ceiling, atCapacity, finished, hungSuspected}`, plus `release()` and `ownedCount`.

`checkpoint.mjs` and `recovery-store.mjs` use `import.meta.dirname` where the donor used `__dirname` for their default roots. Same 'root relative to the module' semantics; `engines.node` is >=24 so the property exists. The donor's own defaults are only reachable when no `root`/`dir` is given.

`failure-recovery.mjs` exports `RECOVERY_RULES` and `VERIFICATION_GATES`, which the donor kept module-private (the gate names were a type-only import from `./execution-planner`). Reason: the budget table is the thing the Mission asks to be reviewable, and the donor's own test file imports it. Freezing preserves the donor's `Readonly`. Contents are verbatim; a normalised diff of the 12 `CLASS_RULES` pattern lines against the donor shows zero differences.

`repository.mjs` additionally carries a default export mirroring the donor's `module.exports` object, because donor `checkpoint.cjs` consumed it as `const repository = require('./repository.cjs')`. The named exports are what the ported `checkpoint.mjs` uses.

No OS seam was invented where the donor had none. `repository.cjs` and `process-identity.cjs` shell out with a hard `spawnSync('git'|'powershell.exe', ...)`; that is preserved as-is and stated in the module headers. `process-identity.cjs`'s injectable `probeProcessOwner({getProcessIdentity})` seam exists in the donor and is preserved verbatim.
knownDifferences: ONE deliberate behaviour change, and it is the only one: Boss `planRecovery` crashes with a `TypeError` on an unknown failure class (`RECOVERY_RULES[cls]` is undefined and the next line dereferences `.inapplicable`; the donor has no refusal for this). It now throws a named Error: `§33.2: "<class>" is not a recovery failure class (expected one of ...)`. Every donor-class behaviour is unchanged. Recorded here because a Verifier should treat it as the one place where this port is deliberately stricter than its donor.

The requirements-driven Execution DAG (`Codex-Boss src/shared/execution-planner.ts`) is NOT ported. Its `planExecution` consumes a Boss `RequirementsGraph` for which this tree has no producer, so porting it would mean inventing behaviour, which MODE=MIGRATION_ONLY forbids. It is recorded as DEFERRED rather than faked, and `index.mjs` deliberately does not re-export it.

The Boss acceptance-hub family (`acceptance*.ts`, `final-acceptance.ts`, `review.ts`, `verification.ts`, `git-checkpoint.ts`, `fleet.ts`, `repo-world-model.ts`) is NOT ported. Those modules persist through Boss host stores or consume Boss requirement/evidence contracts this tree does not have, and the four `THEME_*` surfaces are Entertainment-domain. Recorded as DEFERRED with their reasons.

`guardian.ts`, `root-authority/*`, `tenx/*`, `node-capabilities` and `capability-graph` are NOT ported: City-wide authority/priority and Capability/Node global truth are explicitly forbidden by this Mission.

DS-Hns `app/sub-worker/**` (worker worktree isolation, `FileOwnershipRegistry`, `filterConflicts`, `mergeFileChanges`, path permissions) is NOT ported. It is the worker-pool mechanism behind 02/02 Worker Gateway (MB-003), not the Foreman's own file-ownership guarantee, which IS ported via `mutation.mjs`'s protected-baseline plus root-confinement `mayWrite` and `locking.mjs`'s single-writer workspace lock.
`app/engineering-host.cjs` is NOT ported: it is the Electron shell wiring, not the engineering runtime.

vectors: the plan type vocabulary is closed and a step outside it is refused
a repair must show the failure before anything is patched: the fix template begins with reproduce
a bounded plan drops further steps and records the bound in reasons rather than silently truncating
no step may outlive the episode deadline it was clamped to
the cursor only moves forward and refuses a step that is not the current one
a step's expects falls back to the exit code and says so when the condition is unusable
expects.failurePresent inverts success: a reproduce step that exits 0 has shown nothing
the failover order is timeout flag, then typed code, then the ordered pattern table, then unknown
the failure signature ignores timestamps, paths, hashes and bare numbers, so the same failure stays the same failure
the repair tracker refuses a blind retry and refuses a hypothesis that already failed
resume is a re-check, not a leap of faith: HEAD drift restarts, a moved workspace refuses, an unchanged world resumes
a checkpoint is whole or absent: a half-written temporary file is never read and a corrupt one never hides a good one
the recovery index refuses a checkpoint outside its directory and refuses to regress to an older sequence
automatic recovery attempts are bounded and the fourth blocks the episode
a live lock is never stolen and a writer that lost the lock cannot release it
an episode may not overwrite the file the user had uncommitted before it started
the plan digest gate refuses a plan edited after checkpointing
the completion gate has named refusals and a check that cannot be performed is a refusal, not a pass
a killed, timed-out or signalled process is never a success
verification evidence older than the last change is not fresh evidence
a project declaring Cargo.toml and package.json is a Rust project, not a Node project
every adapter reports its exact detection score and evidence for its own ecosystem
the §33 recovery ladder budgets are consumed per class and end at a Hard Blocker
a CI failure is classified and repaired for real, and a failed read is never a pass

donorBugsFound: adapters/index.cjs header promises an `inferred: true` flag that `command()` never sets; inference is only labelled through CONFIDENCE.INFERRED. Doc/code mismatch, reproduced as-is.

packageManagerOf() answers 'npm' merely because package.json exists, so nodeAdapter emits `npm ci` with confidence `declared` and evidence 'lockfile for npm' for a project with no lockfile — `npm ci` refuses to run without package-lock.json, and the evidence string is false. Reproduced as-is and pinned by a test.
FINAL_REASONS is exported but read nowhere in app/engineering; a report with result 'REFUSED' plus any progress still continues. Reproduced as-is.
javaAdapter.detect reports evidence 'build.gradle' even when the actual file is build.gradle.kts. Reproduced as-is.
Boss planRecovery has no guard for an unknown failure class (see knownDifferences — this one is the single deliberate divergence).

locking.cjs's comment says 'A live lock is never stolen, however old it is', but its `stale` is `!alive || age > staleAfterMs`, so a lock held by a live process past DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER_MS is reclaimable. Kept byte-for-byte; the port's suite documents both readings.
verifyResume composes reason strings, so a working-tree change surfaces as the doubled 'the working tree changed: the working tree changed'. Cosmetic; reproduced exactly.

checkpoint.cjs's default root resolves to the repository root, so its default checkpoint directory lands under the repository. Unreachable unless no root/dir is given; recorded so a host wiring a default does so deliberately.
